Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge, mapping AP-1 chromatin accessibility
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TNF, wounding, or PMA), let them rest for days to weeks, then profile ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN/ChIP. Persistent accessibility and AP-1 motif occupancy at 'memory' enhancers, along with faster or stronger transcription on re-challenge, would indicate memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during priming versus during memory maintenance
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) FOS, JUN, or ATF3 to remove AP-1 either only during the priming stimulus or only after priming. If depletion at priming prevents memory but depletion afterward does not, AP-1 is needed for establishment. If depletion afterward erases memory, it is needed for maintenance.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of memory-state heritability
ideas.description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC-seq, or live imaging with AP-1 reporters, across cell divisions after priming. Lineage barcoding or sister-cell comparison would show whether AP-1-linked accessibility and expression states are inherited clonally and how long they last.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like activity and chromatin-mark analysis at AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Measure H3K27ac, H3K4me1, nucleosome positioning, and BAF/SWI-SNF recruitment (e.g., BRG1 CUT&Tag) at AP-1 sites before, during, and after the stimulus. Use motif-mutated or dCas9-blocked enhancers to test whether AP-1 binding is required to leave a lasting epigenetic mark.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 activation sufficiency test
ideas.description: Use optogenetic or chemogenetic AP-1 activation (e.g., inducible FOS/JUN or a light-controlled version) in naive cells. Varying the dose and duration, then testing the response to a later stimulus, would show whether AP-1 activity alone is sufficient to create a persistent primed state. Compare the result with a non-AP-1 transcription factor control.
